identity.name: refresh_snapshot
identity.description: Recomputes today's data_quality_snapshots row from live tables — 8 consolidated reads (WF3 F1, Spec 118 §1/§7.1) on one pinned REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY client, plus 6 independently-caught optional reads — and UPSERTs the single row for CURRENT_DATE. RECORDER's own contract (Spec 122 §1.10): record current state every run, never judge value bounds (assert_data_bounds owns that). Runs in ALL 4 chains (permits/coa/sources/deep_scrapes); every chain's own invocation re-upserts the SAME day's row.

why_lock.text: Lock 40 is Spec 47 §A.5's registry id (the 'Maintenance' wave) — this step has carried lock 40 since its own advisory-lock retrofit (3c3e6f84, 2026-04-16) and nothing about the conversion changes it. Confirmed unique repo-wide (commit 1 grounding).

guard_why.text: GAP-2 (schema-prescribed, step.schema.json:104-111) + Finding 1. An IS DISTINCT FROM guard on a 68-column dashboard-snapshot row would compare fresh live-DB counts against yesterday's (or this morning's own earlier chain-run's) counts, which are EXPECTED to differ on almost every column, almost every run — permit counts change constantly. A change guard on a metrics-recording row is close to vacuous by construction: the 'change' IS the row's entire purpose. Grandfathered in scripts/steps/_schema/grandfathered.json (Rule 9), mirroring the pre-filed fixture_grandfathered_snapshot fixture's own reasoning verbatim (commit 9e2da7b1, Spec 122 V7).

guard_columns_why.text: LG-9 escape hatch, moot here — guard is "none", so guard_columns is never consulted to build an IS DISTINCT FROM clause.

idempotent_rerun_why.text: Every declared column is rewritten every run, by design — a same-day re-run always rewrites (live counts drift between runs). Explicitly NOT the "zero_writes" default every other class defaults to.

why.text: LG-27 (this pilot, Fold B RULING). A single INSERT...ON CONFLICT...DO UPDATE, no batching — the whole write is one statement inside one pipeline.withTransaction. compute authors the statement text (buildWriteSql) because the key column is a server-side CURRENT_DATE literal, not a bound value, and several columns are JSONB-aggregated across 8+ prior reads — not expressible as the DEFAULT (unnamed) guarded_upsert codegen, which always binds the key as a parameter and always appends a guard clause.

ONE write statement — the single INSERT...ON CONFLICT (snapshot_date) DO UPDATE. write_inventory.statements counts WRITE (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) statements only, per step.schema.json's own description, confirmed against every landed descriptor's convention. This step's 8 pinned-client SELECTs + 6 optional SELECTs are reads and do not count — the smallest write surface of any pilot to date (16 total DML statements enumerated in the plan's own disposition table, all but #16 are reads).

on_check_error_why.text: Every check reads a value the library already measured — a check that throws is a library defect, not an upstream condition. It must redden the run, not drop its row.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*)::int AS c FROM (SELECT snapshot_date FROM data_quality_snapshots GROUP BY snapshot_date HAVING count(*) > 1) d

why.text: INV-1 (plan's own Validator surface section). Mirrors the live UNIQUE(snapshot_date) DB constraint as a declared, observable check rather than an implicit reliance on the constraint alone (Rule 1, nothing hidden). Measured clean on all 5 commit-5 golden captures.

limitations.what: Finding 6 — compute_cost_estimates.js writes 2 columns (cost_estimates_liar_gate_overrides, cost_estimates_zero_total_bypass) into data_quality_snapshots via a best-effort UPDATE, order-dependent on chain position — a cascade this step does not own and correctly does not claim in its own writes[]/emitMeta.
limitations.measured: Live: 4/10 most recent rows NULL on both columns (compute_cost_estimates runs before refresh_snapshot creates that day's row on the first chain run of any given day).

limitations.what: Finding 7 — src/lib/quality/metrics.ts's captureDataQualitySnapshot() (POST /api/quality/refresh, the admin 'Refresh Now' button) is a second, independent implementation of this exact logic, parallel-query-shaped (the pre-WF3-F1 pathology), no advisory lock, 61 of the same 68 columns. Cross-Domain, out of this pilot's Operating Boundary — filed review_followups.md HIGH.
limitations.measured: Live: 0 advisory-lock hits in metrics.ts/route.ts; 61 vs 68 column-list diff confirmed.

recovery.reset: No TRUNCATE/rebuild mechanism exists — a re-run re-derives the full row from live tables every time, which IS the correct reset behaviour for a class that overwrites unconditionally (guard:"none").

interrupted_why.text: No destructive retraction target exists on this step (retract:"none") — there is nothing for an interrupted run to leave half-retracted. A crashed mid-write run simply leaves yesterday's row (or no row) for today; a re-run recomputes the whole row from scratch, which is the same normal-run behaviour, not a special recovery path.

before_image_why.text: R-M's scope is destructive retraction (a DELETE, or an UPDATE overwriting a value with no record of the prior one under conditions where the guard predicate could be wrong) — this write is an idempotent keyed upsert, retract:"none", guard:"none" by design (the row is EXPECTED to differ every run). Unlike CC-D3's centroid repair (which overwrites a value it cannot re-derive without a live recomputation and needed a before-image audit trail), this step's every column is re-derived FRESH from live source tables on every single run — there is no value here that a before-image would let an operator recover that a simple re-run does not already recover identically.

why.text: The normal, and only steady-state, outcome: a RECORDER always has work (recording current state IS the work) — verdict is always PASS, matching Spec 122 :1112's own citation.
A WARN row stands (optional_query_failed or duplicate_snapshot_date_count) and nothing FAILED — the run completed and wrote; the warning is in the table.
Advisory lock 40 is held by another process — a row-derived SKIP summary, never a bare SDK skip with no audit_table.
T1/T2 resolved outside its bounds under on_invalid:"fail". hoisted_above_gate puts this refusal ABOVE the advisory lock.
The one write statement itself failed (a genuine DB error, not an optional-read failure — those carry forward instead of failing the run).

WF3 2026-09-18 (Spec 118 cause B). One of the 8 main reads exceeded refresh_snapshot_read_statement_timeout_minutes, or the reads collectively exceeded refresh_snapshot_phase_deadline_minutes (a wall-clock bound over the whole read loop, armed via pg_cancel_backend on a dedicated connection — EP-PHASE-DEADLINE's mechanism, generalized to the recorder shape). The thrown error names the offending read key, the elapsed ms and which bound fired (statement_timeout vs phase_deadline vs lock_timeout) — no audit_table is built because the failure happens before compute() ever runs; the named error_message on the failed pipeline_runs ledger row is the loud, diagnosable record (mirrors failed_write's own pre-compute throw shape).
